questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Asymptotes of a Hyperbola Given Its Equation in Non-Standard Form
questions.problem: Find the asymptotes of the hyperbola $9{x}^{2}-16{y}^{2}=144.$
questions.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{b}{a}x.
$$

To rewrite the given equation in standard form, we divide both sides of the equation by $144$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{x}^{2}-16{y}^{2} & =144 \\ \frac{9{x}^{2}}{144}-\frac{16{y}^{2}}{144} & =\frac{144}{144} \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{16}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have $a=\sqrt{16}=4,$ and $b=\sqrt{9}=3.$ 

Therefore, the asymptotes are $y=\pm \frac{3}{4}x.$

questions.problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $9{x}^{2}-25{y}^{2}=225.$
questions.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{b}{a}x.
$$

To rewrite the given equation in standard form, we divide both sides of the equation by $225$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{x}^{2}-25{y}^{2} & =225 \\ \frac{9{x}^{2}}{225}-\frac{25{y}^{2}}{225} & =\frac{225}{225} \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{25}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have $a=\sqrt{25}=5,$ and $b=\sqrt{9}=3.$ 

Therefore, the asymptotes are $y=\pm \frac{3}{5}x.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Asymptotes of a Vertical Hyperbola Given in Standard Form
questions.problem: Find the asymptotes of the hyperbola $\frac{{y}^{2}}{64}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{a}{b}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
a=\sqrt{64}=8,\,b=\sqrt{4}=2.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\pm \frac{8}{2}x \\  & =\pm 4x.\end{aligned}
$$
